extraction.name: LongBench
extraction.description: LongBench is a bilingual, multi-task benchmark for long context understanding, comprising 21 datasets across 6 task categories in both English and Chinese, with an average length of 6,711 words for English and 13,386 characters for Chinese. Tasks cover single-doc QA, multi-doc QA, summarization, few-shot learning, synthetic tasks, and code completion, standardized into a unified format for automatic evaluation.
extraction.creator: Yushi Bai, Xin Lv, Jiajie Zhang, Hongchang Lyu, Jiankai Tang, Zhidian Huang, Zhengxiao Du, Xiao Liu, Aohan Zeng, Lei Hou, Yuxiao Dong, Jie Tang, Juanzi Li
extraction.rai:dataCollection: LongBench consists of 21 datasets: 6 are directly extracted from original datasets of previous studies, 10 are built based on original datasets and adapted for long context evaluation, and 5 are newly created and annotated. MultiFieldQA datasets were curated by collecting documents from multiple sources (Arxiv, C4, WuDaoCorpora, Chinese Judgements Online, Wikipedia, and Chinese Government Website). Synthetic tasks were constructed from English Wikipedia and the Chinese C4 dataset. Code completion datasets were sampled and adapted from LCC and RepoBench-P.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Document analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Literature and film scripts (NarrativeQA), scientific NLP papers from Qasper, Arxiv, C4 Dataset, WuDaoCorpora, Chinese Judgements Online, Wikipedia, Chinese Government Website (MultiFieldQA), Wikipedia (HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA, MuSiQue, TriviaQA, PassageCount, PassageRetrieval-en), Baidu Search and Baidu Zhidao (DuReader), U.S. GAO and CRS government reports (GovReport), meeting transcripts (QMSum, VCSUM), news articles (MultiNews, LSHT), web questions (TREC), dialogue transcripts (SAMSum), and GitHub repositories (LCC, RepoBench-P).
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For multi-document QA, complete Wikipedia passages encompassing supporting and distracting paragraphs were concatenated up to a maximum length and randomly ordered; for DuReader, distractors were selected until each question had 20 documents. For MultiNews, 'Document i' was prefixed before the ith article. For few-shot tasks, a random number of examples were sampled from training sets and concatenated into the context. For synthetic PassageRetrieval, 30 passages were sampled and one was summarized. For PassageCount, Wikipedia passages were randomly repeated and shuffled. For RepoBench-P, cross-file code snippets were shuffled with preceding in-file code.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data were extracted from the test sets of public datasets to avoid test leakage (except VCSUM where test data was insufficient). Two sampling strategies were applied: random sampling to maintain natural length distribution for LongBench, and uniform sampling across length ranges (0-4k, 4k-8k, 8k+) for LongBench-E. TriviaQA passages under 1,000 words were filtered for few-shot examples, and long segments from VCSUM were selected.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For MultiFieldQA (English and Chinese), three annotators proposed one question and groundtruth answer per document adhering to guidelines requiring clear questions, definitive and relatively short answers, varied question types, and random distribution of evidence paragraphs. For synthetic PassageRetrieval tasks, paragraph summaries were generated using GPT-3.5-Turbo.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Cross-validation among annotators showed a 100% accuracy rate of the annotated answers in MultiFieldQA.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Three Ph.D. students with extensive research experience in the field of NLP (expert annotators).
extraction.rai:dataBiases: In MultiFieldQA annotation, evidence paragraph placement was kept fairly random to avoid positional biases (such as answer-related statements appearing predominantly at the beginning or end). The paper also notes biases present when using LLMs as evaluation metrics.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Automatic evaluation metrics (ROUGE-L, F1) may not accurately reflect response quality, especially for models generating longer responses; performance on LongBench is coupled with the models' instruction-following capabilities.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking and evaluating large language models on long context understanding and modeling capabilities across different context lengths, task categories, and languages.
